You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the background into a basketball court
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image show a basketball court as the background, with recognizable court features such as a playing surface and court markings or basketball equipment?
node.criteria: Pass if the background is visibly a basketball court with recognizable court features. Fail if the background is clearly not a basketball court. Unknown if the background or its features cannot be assessed reliably.
node.binding: The requested outcome is to replace the image background with a basketball court; judge the edited image against that outcome.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image shows a basketball court background, including a hoop and net, basketballs, and visible court markings on the playing surface.

fulfillment: The node’s binding is too vague and its completion criterion is inconsistent with the evidence: s1 describes a recognizable court with a hoop and markings, while s2 explicitly says the court is not fully complete. Preserve the rubric’s distinction between complete fulfillment and partial progress; do not let s1 passing alone establish completion when another support reports incompleteness. Clarify how the supports jointly establish completion, partial progress, or unresolved evidence, while treating the source image as context for the requested background replacement. The edited image visibly has a hoop, basketballs, and court markings, so the disagreement is about the completion threshold, not absence of requested progress. The aggregate yes label is not atomic ground truth; avoid changing the criterion merely to force agreement. No transport or schema failure is indicated.
s2: The trace clearly supports progress toward the requested background replacement: the kitchen is gone and a basketball hoop, balls, and court markings are visible. The node asks only whether change has begun, so its pass is consistent with its criterion; it does not establish complete fulfillment. Keep this support narrowly scoped to partial progress, and ensure the fulfillment decision combines it with a distinct completion assessment rather than treating this pass as proof that the request is fully complete. Clarify how conflicting completion evidence is resolved without letting a partial-progress check override it. The image evidence is strong, not a transport, schema, or dependency failure; the aggregate label alone does not settle the completion threshold.
